key_insight: A policy mirror descent method can still converge linearly in regularized MDPs even when the critic is updated only once per step via TD, provided the analysis accounts for persistent critic error with a refined potential argument.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more practical actor-critic template for large-scale reinforcement learning because it reduces dependence on exact policy evaluation, resets, and nested inner loops.
method: Exact coordinate-wise Bellman updates prove global linear convergence for finite discounted MDPs.
A resolvent-based auxiliary distribution and decaying Bellman-violation correction control persistent critic error.
For stochastic off-policy learning, finite-batch TD with strongly convex mirror maps yields an \u03b5 value gap using constant stepsizes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an expected value gap of \u03b5 after ~O(1/((1-\u03b3)^5 \u03c3~_b \u03b5)) transitions and says numerical results match the convergence theory.
watch_item: The stochastic guarantee depends on behavior-policy coverage and a finite-batch TD update, so performance may degrade if exploration coverage is weak or batches are too small.
paper_title: Fast Regularized Policy Mirror Descent with One-Step TD Updates
